claims.text: Pronounced lattice distortions in high-entropy alloys create heterogeneous barriers to dislocation glide.
Dislocations in high-entropy alloys undergo intermittent pinning and depinning from local heterogeneities.
Dynamic pinning and depinning cause a transient flow-stress peak immediately after yield.
Formation of entangled dislocation networks after the transient peak enhances ductility.
Evolution of dislocation density and local dislocation entanglement mediates the transition from transient strengthening to ductile behavior.
Formation of stacking faults mediates the transition from transient strengthening to ductile behavior.
Spatially varying energy barriers produced by severe lattice distortion hinder dislocation glide.
Intermittent dislocation pinning at the onset of plasticity causes a transient increase in flow stress.
Dislocation multiplication and entanglement allow the alloy to accommodate more strain while retaining high strength.
The early transient flow-stress peak will be more pronounced in samples with lower initial dislocation densities.
Dislocation entanglement and stacking-fault formation will produce a pronounced stress drop after the early transient peak.
The proposed sequence will result in greater ductility than in a conventional-alloy baseline.
Conventional alloys or HEAs with a more uniform initial dislocation structure exhibit a smoother transition into plastic flow without a marked transient flow-stress spike.
The mechanism applies to near-equiatomic HEAs at moderate strain rates from approximately 300 K to 900 K.
The mechanism may not apply fully to nanocrystalline HEAs with extremely high grain-boundary densities.
The mechanism may not apply under strain rates outside typical in situ testing ranges.
A lack of mobile dislocations at the onset of plastic deformation causes transient mechanical behavior.
Dislocation multiplication and tangling after yield are associated with a rapid increase in strain-hardening rate.
Regions with high pre-existing dislocation density weaken the observed transient behavior.
